label: Map icon itself
summary: Going by its name, gives back the combat map icon it is called on, unchanged.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla lines that use the same name on other types pass it as an argument, for example `Character.Self` handed to a trait name function, so it works as a way to hand the current object on.

label: Edge itself
summary: Going by its name, gives back the combat prediction edge it is called on, as an object a function or widget can work with.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only uses the same name on another type, `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf`, passed into a function that takes the widget.

label: Edge icon
summary: The icon picture of a combat prediction edge.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `texture` of an icon in the map icon layer, so it names an image. The game does not say what an edge is beyond its name.

label: Edge label
summary: The label text of a combat prediction edge.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it in map icon text with the formats `|P` and `|N`.

label: Edge itself
summary: Going by its name, gives back the combat prediction edge it is called on, unchanged.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla uses `Self` on other types to pass the current object into a function, for example `Character.Self`.

label: Prediction icon itself
summary: Going by its name, gives back the combat prediction map icon it is called on, as an object a function or widget can work with.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only uses the same name on another type, `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf`.

label: Attacker character
summary: Going by its name, the character of the attacking side of the predicted combat.
details: The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it on this type. The declare war window has a function of the same name for its own attacker.

label: Attacker edges
summary: Going by its name, the list of prediction edges on the attacker's side.
details: The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it.

label: Defender character
summary: Going by its name, the character of the defending side of the predicted combat.
details: The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it on this type. The declare war window has a function of the same name for its own defender.

label: Defender edges
summary: Going by its name, the list of prediction edges on the defender's side.
details: The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it.

label: Enemy side character
summary: Going by its name, the character on the enemy side of the predicted combat.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `datacontext` of a part of the map icon, so that part then shows this object. That it is a character, and the enemy is seen from the player, comes from the name and the matching player side function.

label: Enemy side edges
summary: Going by its name, the list of prediction edges for the enemy side of the predicted combat.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `datamodel` of a list in the map icon, so the icon draws one entry per list item. That the items are prediction edges comes from the name.

label: Prediction header
summary: The header text of a combat prediction map icon.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it as the `text` of a label in the map icon layer.

label: Player side character
summary: Going by its name, the character on the player's side of the predicted combat.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `datacontext` of a part of the map icon, so that part then shows this object. That it is a character comes from the name.

label: Player side edges
summary: Going by its name, the list of prediction edges for the player's side of the predicted combat.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `datamodel` of a list in the map icon, so the icon draws one entry per list item. That the items are prediction edges comes from the name.

label: Prediction level frame
summary: A whole number that picks which frame of an icon image to show for the prediction level.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `frame` of an icon in the map icon layer, so each prediction level gets its own picture frame.

label: Prediction score
summary: Going by its name, a number that scores the predicted combat.
details: It returns a fixed point number. The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it.

label: Prediction text
summary: The text that describes the combat prediction on a map icon.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it as the `text` of a label in the map icon layer.

label: Temporary info text
summary: Going by its name, a text with temporary information about the prediction icon.
details: It returns text. The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it.

label: Prediction icon itself
summary: Going by its name, gives back the combat prediction map icon it is called on, unchanged.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla uses `Self` on other types to pass the current object into a function, for example `Character.Self`.

label: Result data itself
summary: Going by its name, gives back the combat result data it is called on, as an object a function or widget can work with.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only uses the same name on another type, `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf`.

label: Player gold gain
summary: How much gold the player gained from the combat.
details: Returns a number. Vanilla shows it in the battle summary window, written as a whole number (`|0`). A `PlayerGotGold` check decides whether that line is shown at all.

label: Player piety gain
summary: How much piety the player gained from the combat.
details: Returns a number. Vanilla shows it in the battle summary window, written as a whole number (`|0`). A `PlayerGotPiety` check decides whether that line is shown at all.

label: Player prestige gain
summary: How much prestige the player gained from the combat.
details: Returns a number. Vanilla shows it in the battle summary window, written as a whole number (`|0`). A `PlayerGotPrestige` check decides whether that line is shown at all.

label: War contribution
summary: A whole number: how much the combat changed the given player's war contribution.
details: Vanilla passes `GetPlayer` and shows the result in the battle summary and in a tooltip reading "War Contribution changed by". A `GotWarContribution` check with the same argument tells whether there was a change.

label: Got war contribution
summary: Whether the given character gained war contribution from the battle, going by its name.
details: Takes a character. Vanilla passes the player (`GetPlayer`) and uses it to show a part of the battle summary window.

label: Player got gold
summary: Whether the player gained gold from the combat.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to show or hide the gold gain line in the battle summary window.

label: Player got piety
summary: Whether the player gained piety from the combat.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to show or hide the piety gain line in the battle summary window.

label: Player got prestige
summary: Whether the player gained prestige from the combat.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it to show or hide the prestige gain line in the battle summary window.

label: Player won as main participant
summary: Going by its name, whether the player is a primary war participant on the winning side.
details: It returns yes or no. The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it.

label: Player leads winners
summary: Whether the player is the war leader of the side that won the battle, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it in the battle summary window to show one part when yes and another when not.

label: Result data itself
summary: Going by its name, gives back the combat result data it is called on, unchanged.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla uses `Self` on other types to pass the current object into a function, for example `Character.Self`.

label: Combat side itself
summary: Going by its name, gives back the combat side it is called on, as an object a function or widget can work with.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only uses the same name on another type, `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf`.

label: Custom text
summary: Text from a named custom text of the game, run for this combat side.
details: Returns text. The argument is the name of a custom text. Vanilla never calls it on a combat side; the same name on characters is used a lot, as in `Character.Custom( 'AIEconomicPersonality' )`.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the custom text to run.

label: Side composition
summary: The troop composition of a combat side.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `datacontext` of parts of the combat window, and a tooltip line calls `GetSoldierCountString` on it. So it is a separate object describing the side's troops.

label: Current fighting men
summary: How many soldiers of this side are still fighting.
details: Returns a number. Vanilla shows it in the combat window as a whole number (`|0`), and in tooltips next to the word soldiers.

label: Hard casualties
summary: How many soldiers of this side are dead.
details: Returns a number. A combat window tooltip shows it right after the term "dead soldiers", as a whole number. Vanilla calls it through the left or right combat side of the combat window.

label: Pursuing or retreating label
summary: A text label saying whether the side of a battle is pursuing or retreating.
details: Vanilla shows it in the combat window for the left and the right side. The exact words are not shown in the input.

label: Men in pursuit phase
summary: Going by its name, how many soldiers of this side are in the pursuit phase of the combat.
details: It returns a number. The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it.

label: Soft casualties
summary: How many soldiers of this side are routed, a count separate from the dead.
details: Returns a number. A combat window tooltip shows it after the term "routed soldiers", as a whole number, next to the dead soldiers count. Vanilla calls it through the left or right combat side of the combat window.

label: Is attacker
summary: Whether this side is the attacker of the combat.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla passes it into combat window functions that choose the left or right character and the title of the current battle event.

label: Is still fighting
summary: Whether this side is still fighting in the combat.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it in the combat window to show or hide parts, combined with the pursuit phase check. For example, a part is shown in the pursuit phase only for a side that is no longer fighting.

label: Combat side itself
summary: Going by its name, gives back the combat side it is called on, unchanged.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla uses `Self` on other types to pass the current object into a function, for example `Character.Self`.

label: Side result itself
summary: Going by its name, gives back the result data of one combat side it is called on, as an object a function or widget can work with.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only uses the same name on another type, `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf`.

label: Side's commander
summary: The commander of one side in a finished battle.
details: The game names no return type. Vanilla's battle summary window makes it the data context of the left and right sides' commander displays.

label: Starting soldiers
summary: How many soldiers one side had at the start of the battle, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it as a whole number in the battle summary window for the left and the right side.

label: Loss share
summary: The share of its soldiers one side lost in the battle, as a decimal number.
details: Vanilla uses it as the fill of a bar in the battle summary window for the left and the right side. Whether it runs from 0 to 1 or to 100 is not shown.

label: Side's main participant
summary: The main participant of one side in a battle's result.
details: The game names no return type. Vanilla makes it the data context of map icon parts for the left and the right side of a battle. Who the main participant is is not described.

label: Lost soldiers
summary: How many soldiers one side lost in the battle, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it as a whole number in the battle summary window for the left and the right side.

label: Surviving soldiers
summary: How many soldiers of one side survived the battle, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it as a whole number in the battle summary window for the left and the right side.

label: Regiment stats
summary: Going by its name, the statistics of the regiments of this side.
details: The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it.

label: Side result itself
summary: Going by its name, gives back the side result data it is called on, unchanged.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla uses `Self` on other types to pass the current object into a function, for example `Character.Self`.

label: Combat window itself
summary: Going by its name, gives back the combat window it is called on, as an object a function or widget can work with.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only uses the same name on another type, `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf`.

label: Battle event is shown
summary: Whether the combat window is currently showing a battle event.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it as the `visible` condition of a part of the combat window.

label: Close and deselect
summary: Going by its name, closes the combat window and deselects the combat.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when a button is clicked (`onclick`). What it closes and deselects is read from the name.

label: Combat advantage
summary: A number telling how large the advantage in the combat is.
details: Vanilla shows it with a sign (`|+0=`) and compares it with the value 40 to decide which parts of the window are visible. Which side holds the advantage is not stated in the input.

label: Advantage description
summary: A text describing the advantage in the combat.
details: Returns text. Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the combat window.

label: Advantage position
summary: Going by its name, the position of the advantage marker in the combat window.
details: The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it.

label: Combat
summary: The combat this window shows.
details: The result is a combat object, so more functions can follow it, as in `CombatWindow.GetCombat.PhaseFrozenInfo` in a phase tooltip.

label: Current battle event
summary: The battle event the combat window is showing right now.
details: The result is a battle event, which has a title. Vanilla uses it as the `datacontext` of a part of the window and asks for the title with `GetTitle( ... )`, passing whether the left side is the attacker.

label: Current phase tooltip
summary: A tooltip text about the phase the combat is in now.
details: Returns text. Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the combat window.

label: Left combat side
summary: The combat side shown on the left of the combat window.
details: The result is a combat side, so more functions can follow, such as the number of fighting men, the casualties or the composition. Vanilla uses it a lot in texts and in the window.

label: Left commander traits
summary: Going by its name, the list of traits of the commander on the left side.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `datamodel` of a list in the combat window and checks the list's size against 3 to decide what is visible. That the items are traits comes from the name.

label: Left knight breakdown
summary: A text breaking down the knights on the left side.
details: Returns text. Vanilla uses it in a tooltip of the left side's knight count.

label: Left knight count
summary: How many knights the left side has in the combat.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla writes it next to the knight icon and the culture's word for knights.

label: Left roll
summary: The current roll of the left side.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla shows it as text in the combat window and in a tooltip headed "Current Roll", which also lists the breakdown.

label: Left roll breakdown
summary: A text listing what makes up the left side's current roll.
details: Returns text. Vanilla places it under the "Current Roll" line in a tooltip.

label: Left attack or defend frame
summary: Going by its name, a whole number that picks the attacker or defender icon frame for the left side.
details: The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it.

label: Left attack or defend tooltip
summary: Going by its name, the tooltip text saying whether the left side attacks or defends.
details: It returns text. The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it.

label: Left side commander
summary: The character who commands the left side.
details: The result is a character. Vanilla uses it as the `datacontext` of a part of the combat window, which then shows that character.

label: Left commander tooltip
summary: A tooltip text about the commander on the left side.
details: Returns text. Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the combat window.

label: Left men-at-arms types
summary: The list of men-at-arms types on the left side.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `datamodel` of a list in the combat window, and an emptiness check on it controls what is visible. Reading "MaA" as men-at-arms comes from the game's usual naming.

label: Left main participant
summary: The main character taking part on the left side.
details: The result is a character. Vanilla asks it for the culture's word for knights, in the knight count texts.

label: Left realm flag tooltip
summary: A tooltip text for the realm flag of the left side.
details: Returns text. Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the combat window.

label: Left side relation
summary: Going by its name, a short text naming the left side's relation, used at the start of tooltip lines.
details: Returns text. Vanilla writes it with the `|U` format (first letter capitalized) before terms such as soldiers, routed soldiers and dead soldiers. What the words are, and relative to whom, is not shown in the input.

label: Left terrain and holding effects
summary: Going by its name, a text listing the terrain and holding effects that work for the left side.
details: It returns text. The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it.

label: Combat name
summary: The name of the combat shown in the window.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it as the window's text. The name is used very often on other types, so treat it as a hint only.

label: Power position
summary: Going by its name, the position of the power marker in the combat window.
details: The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it.

label: Retreat tooltip
summary: Going by its name, the tooltip text about retreating from the combat.
details: It returns text. The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it.

label: Right combat side
summary: The combat side shown on the right of the combat window.
details: The result is a combat side, so more functions can follow, such as the number of fighting men or the casualties. Vanilla uses it in texts and in the window.

label: Right commander traits
summary: Going by its name, the list of traits of the commander on the right side.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `datamodel` of a list in the combat window and checks the list's size against 3 to decide what is visible. That the items are traits comes from the name.

label: Right knight breakdown
summary: A text breaking down the knights on the right side.
details: Returns text. Vanilla uses it in a tooltip of the right side's knight count.

label: Right knight count
summary: How many knights the right side has in the combat.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla writes it next to the knight icon and the culture's word for knights.

label: Right roll
summary: The current roll of the right side.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla shows it as text in the combat window and in a tooltip headed "Current Roll", which also lists the breakdown.

label: Right roll breakdown
summary: A text listing what makes up the right side's current roll.
details: Returns text. Vanilla places it under the "Current Roll" line in a tooltip.

label: Right attack or defend frame
summary: Going by its name, a whole number that picks the attacker or defender icon frame for the right side.
details: The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it.

label: Right attack or defend tooltip
summary: Going by its name, the tooltip text saying whether the right side attacks or defends.
details: It returns text. The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it.

label: Right side commander
summary: The character who commands the right side.
details: The result is a character. Vanilla uses it as the `datacontext` of a part of the combat window, which then shows that character.

label: Right commander tooltip
summary: A tooltip text about the commander on the right side.
details: Returns text. Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the combat window.

label: Right men-at-arms types
summary: The list of men-at-arms types on the right side.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `datamodel` of a list in the combat window, and an emptiness check on it controls what is visible. Reading "MaA" as men-at-arms comes from the game's usual naming.

label: Right main participant
summary: The main character taking part on the right side.
details: The result is a character. Vanilla asks it for the culture's word for knights, in the knight count texts.

label: Right realm flag tooltip
summary: A tooltip text for the realm flag of the right side.
details: Returns text. Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the combat window.

label: Right side relation
summary: Going by its name, a short text naming the right side's relation, used at the start of tooltip lines.
details: Returns text. Vanilla writes it with the `|U` format (first letter capitalized) before terms such as soldiers, routed soldiers and dead soldiers. What the words are, and relative to whom, is not shown in the input.

label: Right terrain and holding effects
summary: Going by its name, a text listing the terrain and holding effects that work for the right side.
details: It returns text. The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it.

label: Won or lost label
summary: A text saying whether the combat was won or lost.
details: Returns text. Vanilla shows it as a label in the combat window. That it says won or lost comes from the name.

label: Go to province
summary: Moves the map view to the province where the combat takes place.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when a button is clicked (`onclick`). The province being the combat's is read from the name.

label: Has combat ended
summary: Going by its name, whether the combat has ended.
details: It returns yes or no. The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it.

label: Has player
summary: Going by its name, whether the player takes part in the combat.
details: It returns yes or no. The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it.

label: Has player lost
summary: Going by its name, whether the player lost the combat.
details: It returns yes or no. The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it.

label: Has player won
summary: Going by its name, whether the player won the combat.
details: It returns yes or no. The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it.

label: Next battle event
summary: Steps the combat window on to the next battle event.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when a button is clicked (`onclick`). The step to the next event is read from the name.

label: Attacker is on left
summary: Whether the attacker is the side shown on the left.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it as a `visible` condition, and also negated with `Not`, to show one layout when the attacker is left and another when it is right.

label: In maneuver phase
summary: Whether the combat is in its maneuver phase.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it as the `visible` condition of a part of the combat window.

label: In pursuit phase
summary: Whether the combat is in its pursuit phase.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it a lot as a `visible` condition, often combined with which side is winning or whether a side is still fighting.

label: Left side is winning
summary: Whether the side on the left is winning the combat.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it as a `visible` condition, alone and with the pursuit phase check.

label: Right side is winning
summary: Whether the side on the right is winning the combat.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it as a `visible` condition, alone and with the pursuit phase check.

label: Left has terrain effects
summary: Going by its name, whether the left side has terrain or holding effects.
details: It returns yes or no. The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it.

label: Right has terrain effects
summary: Going by its name, whether the right side has terrain or holding effects.
details: It returns yes or no. The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it.

label: Combat window itself
summary: Going by its name, gives back the combat window it is called on, unchanged.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla uses `Self` on other types to pass the current object into a function, for example `Character.Self`.

label: Show no-retreat icon
summary: Whether the combat window should show the icon for a combat that cannot be retreated from.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it as the `visible` condition of an icon. The meaning of the icon is read from the name.

label: Show retreat icon
summary: Whether the combat window should show the retreat icon.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it as the `visible` condition of an icon.

label: Command itself
summary: Going by its name, gives back the command it is called on, as an object a function or widget can work with.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only uses the same name on another type, `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf`.

label: Command itself
summary: Going by its name, gives back the command it is called on, unchanged.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla uses `Self` on other types to pass the current object into a function, for example `Character.Self`.

label: Recorder itself
summary: Going by its name, gives back the command recorder it is called on, as an object a function or widget can work with.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only uses the same name on another type, `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf`.

label: Inbox size
summary: How many entries wait in the command recorder's inbox, as a whole number, going by its name.
details: The command recorder is a debug tool of the engine that records the commands of a session. Vanilla shows this number in its panel. What waits in the inbox is not described.

label: Recorded command count
summary: How many commands the command recorder has recorded, as a whole number.
details: Shown in the session recorder panel, a debug tool of the engine.

label: Recorded command
summary: One recorded command, picked by its position in the recording.
details: Takes a position (a whole number). The game names no return type. Vanilla's session recorder panel passes the selected item's position and shows the command's token.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The position of the command in the recording.

label: Recorded commands
summary: The list of commands the command recorder has recorded.
details: The game names no return type. Vanilla fills the list of the session recorder panel, a debug tool of the engine, from it.

label: Is recording
summary: Whether the command recorder is recording right now.
details: Vanilla's session recorder panel shows one part while recording and another while not.

label: Recorder frame update
summary: Updates the command recorder each frame, going by its name, and returns yes or no.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility condition of the whole session recorder panel, which makes the interface call it again and again. What the yes or no means is not described.

label: Recorder itself
summary: Going by its name, gives back the command recorder it is called on, unchanged.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla uses `Self` on other types to pass the current object into a function, for example `Character.Self`.

label: Recorder panel itself
summary: Going by its name, gives back the dockable panel of the command recorder it is called on, as an object a function or widget can work with.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only uses the same name on another type, `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf`.

label: Selected item position
summary: The position of the item selected in the session recorder panel, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in the panel and passes it on to pick the matching recorded command.

label: Has selected item
summary: Whether an item is selected in the session recorder panel.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the panel's part for the selected item only when there is one.

label: Select item
summary: Selects the item at a given position in the session recorder panel.
details: Returns nothing. Vanilla runs it when an entry of the list is clicked, passing that entry's position (`PdxGuiWidget.GetIndexInDataModel`).

label: Recorder panel itself
summary: Going by its name, gives back the command recorder panel it is called on, unchanged.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla uses `Self` on other types to pass the current object into a function, for example `Character.Self`.

label: Bar itself
summary: Going by its name, gives back the complex bar it is called on, as an object a function or widget can work with.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only uses the same name on another type, `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf`.

label: Current filled width
summary: Going by its name, a whole number giving the width share of the filled part of the bar.
details: Vanilla uses it as a `layoutstretchfactor_horizontal`, so it sets how much room the filled part takes next to the other parts of the progress bar.

label: Current left width
summary: A whole number giving the width share of the bar part to the left of the current value.
details: Vanilla uses it as a `layoutstretchfactor_horizontal` in the progress bar layout. Which part exactly is read from the name.

label: Current right width
summary: A whole number giving the width share of the bar part to the right of the current value.
details: Vanilla uses it as a `layoutstretchfactor_horizontal` in the progress bar layout. Which part exactly is read from the name.

label: Current value
summary: The value the bar currently shows.
details: Returns a number. Vanilla puts it in tooltips, for example the level track of a trait and the infection rate of an epidemic (shown as a percentage), and compares it with the neutral value to decide which part of a bar to show.

label: Data width
summary: A whole number giving the width share of the data part of the bar.
details: Vanilla uses it as a `layoutstretchfactor_vertical`, so it is used in the vertical progress bars. What counts as the data part is read from the name.

label: Filled width
summary: A whole number giving the width share of the filled part of the bar.
details: Vanilla uses it as a stretch factor in both the horizontal and the vertical progress bars. Its meaning is read from the name.

label: Index of item
summary: The position of a given item within the bar.
details: Returns a whole number. Vanilla passes the item itself (`ComplexBarItem.Self`) and uses the position to pick an accolade rank icon and tooltip.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The bar item to look up.
fields.values: a bar item, as vanilla passes `ComplexBarItem.Self`

label: Bar items
summary: The list of items that make up the bar.
details: Vanilla uses it as the `datamodel` of a progress bar, so one entry is drawn per item, and measures its size to decide what is visible.

label: Left empty width
summary: A whole number giving the width share of the empty space at the left end of the bar.
details: Vanilla uses it as a stretch factor in both the horizontal and the vertical progress bars. Its meaning is read from the name.

label: Left margin
summary: A whole number giving the width share of the margin at the left end of the bar.
details: Vanilla uses it as a `layoutstretchfactor_vertical` in the vertical progress bars. Its meaning is read from the name.

label: Maximum value
summary: Going by its name, the highest value the bar can show.
details: Returns a number. Vanilla uses it in the epidemic window's infection rate tooltip next to the current value.

label: Minimum value
summary: Going by its name, the lowest value the bar can show.
details: Returns a number. Vanilla uses the same name only on another type, a story cycle counter, as a `min` value.

label: Neutral marker left width
summary: A whole number giving the width share to the left of the bar's neutral marker.
details: Vanilla uses it as a stretch factor in both the horizontal and the vertical progress bars, to place the neutral marker.

label: Neutral marker right width
summary: A whole number giving the width share to the right of the bar's neutral marker.
details: Vanilla uses it as a stretch factor in both the horizontal and the vertical progress bars, to place the neutral marker.

label: Neutral value
summary: The value of the bar that counts as neutral.
details: Returns a number. Vanilla compares the current value with it in the personal beliefs window, to show one part when the value is at or above it and another when it is below.

label: Next marker left width
summary: A whole number giving the width share to the left of the bar's next marker.
details: Vanilla uses it as a horizontal stretch factor in the progress bar layout, to place the next marker.

label: Next marker right width
summary: A whole number giving the width share to the right of the bar's next marker.
details: Vanilla uses it as a horizontal stretch factor in the progress bar layout, to place the next marker.

label: Next value
summary: The value at the next step of the bar.
details: Returns a number. Vanilla shows it in a tooltip next to the current experience of a trait level track, and in the infection rate tooltip. What the next step is depends on the bar.

label: Next width
summary: A whole number giving the width share of the part of the bar up to the next value.
details: Vanilla uses it as a horizontal stretch factor in the progress bar layout.

label: Right empty width
summary: A whole number giving the width share of the empty space at the right end of the bar.
details: Vanilla uses it as a stretch factor in both the horizontal and the vertical progress bars. Its meaning is read from the name.

label: Right margin
summary: A whole number giving the width share of the margin at the right end of the bar.
details: Vanilla uses it as a `layoutstretchfactor_vertical` in the vertical progress bars. Its meaning is read from the name.

label: Has valid data
summary: Going by its name, whether the bar has valid data to show.
details: It returns yes or no. The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it.

label: Is decreasing
summary: Whether the bar's value is going down.
details: Returns yes or no. Vanilla uses it as the `visible` condition of a part of the progress bar. That it means a falling value is read from the name.
